newsitem.title: ITALY: Sacrifices still needed for Italy EMU entry - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Sacrifices still needed for Italy EMU entry - Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in an interview published on Wednesday that Italy's chances of being a founder member of the single European currency were more than 100 percent, but that sacrifices still lie ahead.
"A year ago, I said our chances of entering monetary union were 100 percent. Today, if possible, our chances have increased," Prodi said in an interview in Turin's La Stampa newspaper.
"However, the season of sacrifices cannot be considered over, it is long and requires perseverance."

Prodi said his centre-left goverment must in September present a deficit-cutting plan for 1998 that will allow it to slice 25 trillion lire off the state deficit, as indicated in the country's three-year economic strategy, known as the DPEF.
The DPEF, which the government presented in May, says the deficit reduction should be achieved by combining 15 trillion lire of spending cuts with 10 trillion lire of revenue raising measures.
European nations need to comply with the Maastricht financial criteria in order to quality for the single European currency, due to start in 1999.

Ongoing talks between the government, unions and employers on reforming Italy's costly welfare state must also end by September so the reforms can be included in the deficit-trimming plan, Prodi added.
He said his government would launch a plan for economic growth in September, which would include incentives for the construction sector and for companies that sponsor research activities.
"After the summer, the phase of growth will begin. Until now, we have followed a strategy of deficit reduction. Now we have to spur development and limit unemployment."
